notes.description: Replaces the divider in x/x by an all-zero/all-one exponent test driving a mux between 1.0 and NaN — cheap in hardware where it is not in software, and the mux pushes downstream.
source_headings: ## Floating-point optimizations in an HLS context

notes.name: Function Table ROM
notes.description: Tabulate f at every input code in a ROM — the only approximator needing no smoothness at all, at a cost of 2^n·m bits that doubles per input bit.
source_headings: ## A first generic approximator: simple tabulation
### Tabulating precomputed function values in a ROM

notes.name: LUT-Array Function Table
notes.description: A 2^α×n ROM as n α-input LUTs sharing one address bus — the FPGA unit cost, and why shrinking the address below α buys nothing.

notes.name: Synthesized Logic Table
notes.description: Hand the table to standard-cell synthesis as a Boolean function instead of instantiating memory; area 2^(0.65min(k,n))·2^(0.19|k-n|), symmetric in inputs and outputs.

notes.name: Hard ROM Macro
notes.description: Transistor-level ROM: stored bits become wiring to the rails and all the logic is address decoding — lowest cost per bit, but it forfeits logic optimization and measured larger than standard cells.

notes.name: Output Format Widening
notes.description: Fix the range wrap by adding one output MSB — exact and free in logic, but roughly half the output range goes unused and the operator becomes 8-bit in, 9-bit out.

notes.name: Saturating Output Clamp
notes.description: Clamp the unrepresentable top value to the largest representable one — the only range fix that is actual added hardware, and it doubles the error at the two rightmost inputs.

notes.name: Round-Down Table Fill
notes.description: Define the tabulated function as RD(f) rather than RN(f) so the top value can never round up — zero hardware, but the error budget doubles to a full ulp everywhere.

notes.name: Output Range Scaling
notes.description: Tabulate (1-2^l)·f instead of f so the image lands inside the format — free, generic, still perfectly rounded, but against a modified function, so ~1.5 ulp against the original.
source_headings: ## Worked example — 4-bit sin(pi/2 x), and the trap

notes.name: Tabulated Reciprocal
notes.description: 1/x as 2/(x+1)-1 on [0,1): the +1 and -1 are free bit ops, and the one extra MSB that f(0)=1 demands is absorbed by the leading-zero-count and shift reconstruction.

notes.name: Modular Squaring Table
notes.description: Tabulate x^2 mod p to build a modular multiplier from ab=((a+b)^2-(a-b)^2)/4 — a wildly discontinuous function that tabulation handles without noticing.
source_headings: ### Tabulating precomputed function values in a ROM

notes.name: Residual-Sign Rounding Unit
notes.description: Turn any faithful algebraic-function approximation into a correctly rounded one: compute S faithful at precision l-1, and when its LSB is 1 let the sign of P(S,X,Y) pick the neighbour.

notes.name: LDTC, Lossless Differential Table Compression
notes.description: Splits any ROM into a sub-sampling table plus a narrow difference table and one addition, reproducing the original value bit-for-bit at 20-50% of the bits.

notes.name: Bipartite Table Method
notes.description: Replaces one 2^w_X ROM with a table of initial values plus a table of tabulated offsets and one adder — piecewise linear interpolation with the multiplier deleted, at alpha ~ 2w_X/3.
source_headings: ## Where the two tables come from
### From bipartite to multipartite: splitting the TO

notes.name: Symmetric Table of Offsets
notes.description: Two rows of XOR gates exploit the symmetry of a linear segment about its centre, halving the offset table's entries and shaving one output bit — a 4x cut in stored bits for a handful of gates.

notes.name: Multipartite Methods
notes.description: Splits the offset table into m tables, each with its own coarser slope index gamma_i, trading m-1 extra additions for an order-of-magnitude smaller table; bipartite is the m=1 case.
source_headings: ### From bipartite to multipartite: splitting the TO
### Computing the sizes of the sub-tables
### Why multipartite is close to optimal among order-one methods

notes.name: Multipartite with Compressed TIV
notes.description: Runs LDTC on the table of initial values — the dominant term — inside the multipartite search, shrinking the architecture at exactly zero accuracy cost.

notes.name: HUB Table Filling
notes.description: Fills every offset table in HUB format so negation is bitwise complement, then folds the surviving half-ulps into the TIV constant so the final rounding is pure truncation — zero hardware.
source_headings: ### Filling the tables using HUB format

notes.name: Monotonic Multipartite Tables
notes.description: Buys monotonicity back from a faithful operator by taking the right-end slope instead of the averaged chord slope — wider tables and more guard bits, 7.25 KB against 5.5 KB in AMD's K6-2 reciprocal square root.

notes.name: ILP-Optimized Multipartite Tables
notes.description: One ILP variable per table entry and two rounding constraints per input value yields correctly rounded table architectures — 5x fewer LUTs than LDTC at 16 bits, and lower latency than a plain ROM.

notes.name: ATA, Addition-Table-Addition
notes.description: Adds before the lookup as well as after: two reads of one table give f(A) and f(A+B), and their scaled forward difference replaces the derivative table entirely.

notes.name: Central-Difference ATA
notes.description: Three reads of the same table and a centred difference push the error to third order; the same three reads also support a full second-order Taylor form whose extra rounding eats the accuracy it bought.

notes.name: STAM, Symmetric Table Addition Method
notes.description: Wong and Goto's production form: B split in two, two centred differences, plus a second/third-order correction table — 6 tables of 12-13 input bits and 9 additions at 24 bits.

notes.name: Partial Product Array Function Evaluation
notes.description: Flattens a polynomial approximation and all its coefficients into weighted products of input bits, prunes the array, and partitions the survivors into tables — a bit heap that loses the continuity multipartite exploits.

notes.name: Remez Minimax
notes.description: Equioscillating coefficients that beat edge-Taylor by 2^(2d+1) — the same accuracy for d+1 fewer bits of table, at zero hardware cost.
notes.spade_note: Sollya remez(): a numerical exchange algorithm run at generate time. Its output (the coefficients) is hardware; the algorithm is not.

notes.name: Polynomial Coefficient Table
notes.description: The 2^alpha-entry ROM of per-segment coefficients — the only exponential resource in the operator, shrunk by shared LSB, hardwired constant signs and differential compression.

notes.name: Uniform Piecewise Segmentation
notes.description: Splits the input into 2^alpha equal segments by a pure wire split — alpha bits of address, w_X-alpha bits of reduced argument — buying alpha(d+1) bits of accuracy for a 2^alpha-deep table.

notes.name: Logarithmic Segmentation
notes.description: Indexes the coefficient table by leading-zero count, absorbing a discontinuity or infinite derivative at zero — at the price of an LZC, a shifter and an unreduced w_Y.

notes.name: Hierarchical Segmentation
notes.description: Stacks a second uniform level inside each first-level segment (UU) or inside each logarithmic segment (LU), giving logarithmic segmentation the memory/arithmetic knob it otherwise lacks.

notes.name: Dichotomy-Based Segmentation
notes.description: Balances approximation error across arbitrary segments — best possible fit, paid for with a comparator-tree search and a subtractor for Y = X - M_A.

notes.name: Function-Value Interpolation
notes.description: Tabulates function values instead of coefficients and derives the polynomial from neighbours — saves the higher-degree tables but scales backwards with degree, so it loses to tabulated polynomials.

notes.name: Addition-Theorem Coefficient Generation
notes.description: Computes C1..C3 from a single tabulated C0 by constant multiplications, exploiting sin(a+b) — three coefficient tables collapse into one.

notes.name: Horner Evaluation
notes.description: A chain of d truncated multiply-adds whose operands narrow by ~alpha bits per stage — minimal multiplier count and ~26% less multiplier area than uniform widths, at O(d) latency.
source_headings: ### Why every stage gets its own widths

notes.name: Parallel Polynomial Evaluator
notes.description: Evaluates the developed form with all monomials in flight and one compressor tree — O(log d) depth instead of Horner's O(d), for more multipliers.

notes.name: HOTBM
notes.description: Splits each power term into subwords and tabulates C_i(A)*P_k,i against a truncated interval index — the table-based route to a parallel evaluator of any degree.

notes.name: Estrin's Scheme
notes.description: Recursive odd/even split p(x)=p_e(x^2)+x*p_o(x^2): halves Horner's latency at the cost of precomputing x^2 and a little accuracy.

notes.name: SquareRich Evaluation
notes.description: Completes the square to trade one multiplier for a cheaper squarer — but after a uniform reduction the squarer runs on a much wider word than the multiplier it replaced.

notes.name: ILP-Optimized Polynomial Evaluator
notes.description: Makes the coefficient bits ILP variables so approximation and rounding are optimized jointly — correct rounding at 24 bits, not just faithful, with fewer coefficient bits.

notes.name: Floating-Point Polynomial Function Evaluator
notes.description: Wraps a fixed-point polynomial core in exponent handling, and gets a logarithmic segmentation for free because the input exponent is already a crude log2(X).
source_headings: ## Floating-Point Architectures Built on Fixed-Point Polynomials

notes.name: Square Root Range Reduction
notes.description: Forces an even exponent so the square root is a one-bit exponent shift, at the cost of one denormalising shift of the significand into [1,4).
source_headings: ### Range reduction for floating-point and fixed-point binary

notes.name: Restoring Square Root
notes.description: One digit per cycle from a trial subtraction and its sign, undone when negative; cheapest possible selection, at the price of a restore mux in the loop.

notes.name: Non-Restoring Square Root
notes.description: Keeps the tentative remainder as state so the digit is the inverted sign bit; one inverter plus one add/sub of i+4 bits, the FloPoCo default on FPGAs.
source_headings: ## Worked example: $\sqrt{2}$ by binary non-restoring digit recurrence

notes.name: SRT Square Root
notes.description: Redundant digit set plus a carry-save residual cuts the per-iteration carry propagation to a few leading digits, at the cost of an on-the-fly converter and a two-dimensional selection function.
source_headings: ### Exploiting redundant number systems in the square root

notes.name: Square Root Digit Selection Function
notes.description: A LUT reading 4 truncated bits of the carry-save residual and 4 of the partial root; the redundancy overlap is what lets a truncated, one-sided input still pick a legal digit.
source_headings: ### Exploiting redundant number systems in the square root

notes.name: Square Root Seed Table
notes.description: Tabulates S_i0 (and S_i0 squared) from the 8 leading bits of M to skip the first iterations; the width constraint fails outright unless the table rounds to nearest.
source_headings: ### Exploiting redundant number systems in the square root

notes.name: On-the-Fly Converter
notes.description: Carries a pre-decremented copy of the partial result alongside it so a negative redundant digit is absorbed by concatenation; two muxes and two registers per iteration, no adder.
source_headings: ### Exploiting redundant number systems in the square root

notes.name: Digit-Recurrence Cube Root
notes.description: Same recurrence one degree up, with the partial square built by a parallel recurrence so no multiplier appears; twice as slow and twice as small as the multiplier-based cube root, and correctly rounded for free.

notes.name: Digit-Recurrence Euclidean Norm
notes.description: Evaluates sqrt(X^2+Y^2+Z^2) in one recurrence: reorder so X is largest, initialise with it and never compute X squared, accumulating the other two squares one partial-product line per iteration.

notes.name: E-Method
notes.description: A vector digit recurrence solving Ay=b that merges numerator, denominator and division of a rational approximation into one pass with no multiplier and no divider.
source_headings: ## The E-method for evaluating rational functions
### Rational approximations compatible with the E-method

notes.name: Octant Argument Reduction
notes.description: Peel the sign/quadrant/octant bits off a binary angle and fold the rest into [0,1/4) with one row of XORs, so every sin/cos engine only ever sees an octant.

notes.name: Sine-Cosine Octant Reconstruction
notes.description: The output-side swap/negate: eight sqo patterns select which of (sin,cos) goes where and with which sign, at the cost of a mux pair and a row of XORs.

notes.name: CORDIC Rotation Mode
notes.description: Sine and cosine of an angle from three adders and two shifts per step: choosing micro-rotations of arctan(2^-i) makes tan alpha_i a right shift, so a transcendental costs an adder.

notes.name: Unrolled CORDIC
notes.description: n = -l+2 hardwired stages: shifts become routing, arctan constants become literals, and the whole operator is ~2.5(-l+g)^2 LUTs with zero DSP and zero block RAM.
source_headings: ### Approximation error and the number of iterations

notes.name: Reduced-Z CORDIC Datapath
notes.description: |Z_i| < 2^-i, so stage i's angle adder can be one bit narrower than stage i-1's: a triangular instead of rectangular Z datapath, ~1/6 off total area and a shorter d_i path.

notes.name: Iterative CORDIC
notes.description: One stage folded back on itself: n cycles instead of n stages, much lower area, but it pays for two real barrel shifters and an arctan ROM and loses the reduced-Z trick.

notes.name: Reduced-Iteration CORDIC
notes.description: Stop rotating at i = floor(-l/2)+1 and finish the residual rotation with two small multipliers using sin(pi Z) ~ pi Z, cos(pi Z) ~ 1: half the pipeline depth for two DSPs.
source_headings: ### Replacing half the CORDIC iterations with a small multiplier

notes.name: Table-and-Multiplier Sine and Cosine
notes.description: Split the octant angle into a table-addressed head and a tiny tail recombined by the addition formula: three logic levels instead of a chain of -l+2 adders, and g=4 whatever the precision.
source_headings: ## An architecture based on tables and multipliers

notes.name: Small-Angle Taylor Sine and Cosine
notes.description: For Z < 2^-alpha, sin Z ~ Z - Z^3/6 and cos Z ~ 1 - Z^2/2 with power-of-two coefficients; tabulate Z^2/2 and Z^3/6, or build z - z^3/6 in one bit heap with a divide-by-3.

notes.name: Generic Polynomial Sine Evaluator
notes.description: The lazy option: wrap the generic table-and-DSP polynomial evaluator in a quadrant reduction and a sin/cos select bit - one function per instance, not a fused pair.
source_headings: ## An architecture using a generic polynomial evaluator

notes.name: Floating-Point Accumulator Loop
notes.description: The obvious accumulator — an FP adder with its output fed back — and why it fails twice: one summand every l cycles, and error growing as (N-1)u times the sum of magnitudes.
source_headings: ## The problem with the obvious circuit

notes.name: Exact Sum-of-Products Operator
notes.description: The whole composed datapath — exact multiplier, aligner, wide fixed-point accumulator, converter — accepting one (X,Y) pair per cycle with zero summation error.

notes.name: Exact Unnormalized Multiplier
notes.description: A floating-point multiplier that deliberately does not round or normalise: one wide OR handles subnormals, and the doubly biased exponent sum is already the alignment shift distance.

notes.name: Sign-Padding Alignment Shifter
notes.description: The FloatToFix front end: negate on w_F bits before shifting instead of w_A bits after, paid for with a shifter that pads both ends with the sign bit.
source_headings: ### Simple accumulator architectures for small precisions

notes.name: Two's-Complement Exact Accumulator
notes.description: The core loop: aligned summand, XOR row plus carry-in for negation, one w_A-bit adder and register — the only thing left in the feedback path is an integer add.
source_headings: ### Simple accumulator architectures for small precisions

notes.name: Kulisch Accumulator
notes.description: The universal sizing: 277 bits for a binary32 sum, 554 for a sum of products, plus 58 guard bits against spurious overflow — exact on data it has never seen, at ten times the area of an FP adder.

notes.name: Application-Specific Exact Accumulator
notes.description: Three parameters (m_A, l_A, m_X) from physics and profiling collapse 177 bits to 63 — at the price of an overflow comparator and a truncating or rounding shifter that the exact version never needs.
source_headings: ### Simple accumulator architectures for small precisions

notes.name: High-Radix Carry-Save Accumulator
notes.description: Cut the carry propagation every alpha bits and hold each chunk's carry-out in a flip-flop: the critical path becomes alpha bits instead of w_A, for k-1 registers and k flush cycles at the end.

notes.name: Sign-Magnitude Accumulator
notes.description: The rejected alternative — add or subtract by relative sign, then re-negate on zero crossing — which needs a compound adder to keep two w_A-bit carry chains off the loop.
source_headings: ### Simple accumulator architectures for small precisions

notes.name: Accumulator Exception FSM
notes.description: Four states — finite, +inf, -inf, NaN — reproducing an FP adder's behaviour on exceptional inputs alongside a datapath that has no notion of them.
source_headings: ### Simple accumulator architectures for small precisions

notes.name: Accumulator-to-Float Converter
notes.description: FixToFloat for an accumulator inside the output exponent range: leading-sign count and normaliser, XOR negation, exponent E0+m_A-C, and a single adder that rounds and packs at once.
source_headings: ### Conversion of the accumulator back to floating point

notes.name: Three-Zone Accumulator Converter
notes.description: When the accumulator outruns the output exponent range: a wide OR above e_max detects overflow, a wide OR below e_min-w_F feeds the sticky, and only the middle 277 bits reach the normaliser.
source_headings: ### Conversion of the accumulator back to floating point

notes.name: FPExp Operator
notes.description: A complete float-in/float-out exponential: additive range reduction whose 2^E reconstruction is free because it lands straight in the exponent field — at the cost of two constant multipliers held to absolute accuracy 2^{-w_F-g} regardless of how large X is.

notes.name: Exponential Special-Case Unit
notes.description: Three threshold comparisons on the exponent field alone that dispose of +0, +inf and the exact-1.0 region before any arithmetic — coarse enough to be two magnitude compares, with the leftover cases caught later in the packer.

notes.name: Direct Tabulation Exponential
notes.description: The whole exponential as one ROM addressed by exponent-minus-constant concatenated with the fraction — correctly rounded by construction and one BRAM at BFloat, but the table grows as 2^{w_F} and dies above about 8 fraction bits.

notes.name: Split-Table Exponential
notes.description: Scales direct tabulation by splitting X = X_H + X_L and multiplying two tabulated factors — legal and simple, but reconstruction costs a full w_F x w_F multiplier per extra chunk, which is why the book abandons it for range reduction.

notes.name: Exponential Fixed-Point Converter
notes.description: One left barrel shifter plus a constant subtraction on the exponent turns the floating-point input into ufix(w_E-2, -w_F-g) and raises the coarse under/overflow flag — subnormal inputs need no special path because they all fall in the return-1.0 region.

notes.name: Tentative Exponent Unit
notes.description: Computes E = round(X_fix/ln 2) on w_E+1 signed bits from a deliberately sloppy constant multiplier — the whole error budget is 0.22, half of which is spent truncating X_fix to LSB -4 to shrink the multiplier.

notes.name: Reduced Argument Subtractor
notes.description: Y = X_fix - E ln 2 by a KCM that need not compute its own MSBs, because the subtraction is a cancellation by design — few input bits, many output bits, and ln 2 stored to the precision of the product rather than of the format.

notes.name: Exponential Normalize-Round-Pack
notes.description: One multiplexer on the MSB of M, one half-ulp bit, and a single w_E+w_F+1-bit adder across the concatenated exponent-and-significand field — biased formats make rounding overflow increment the exponent for free; IEEEfloat adds a subnormal shifter.

notes.name: Fixed-Point-In Exponential
notes.description: The FPExp datapath entered at X_fix: no unpack, no input shifter, no negate box, and exact guard bits — smaller and more accurate than converting to float first, at the price of signed constant multipliers.

notes.name: Tabulated e^Y
notes.description: After range reduction the inner evaluator can be a single correctly-rounded ROM addressed by Y — 2^10 x 11 bits at BFloat, four times smaller than tabulating the whole operator, but it pays for the range-reduction hardware in front of it.

notes.name: Higher-Order e^Y Evaluator
notes.description: A second, bit-field range reduction Y = A + Z: an e^A table, an h(Z) = e^Z - Z - 1 box that is 2k bits narrower than e^Z, and one near-square truncated multiplier — single precision lands on exactly one BRAM and one DSP.
source_headings: Using large tables and square multipliers

notes.name: First-Order e^Y Evaluator
notes.description: Drops the h box entirely, approximating f(Z) by Z: one e^A table, one small multiplier, one adder, and g=3 still holds — but k must be about (w_F+4)/2, so the table grows as 2^{w_F/2} and it stops at binary16.

notes.name: Polynomial h(Z) Evaluator
notes.description: Replaces the h box with a generic piecewise-polynomial evaluator on [0,1] — k and the degree d become two independent knobs instead of one, which is what carries the architecture to double precision (k=9, d=2, 512 intervals).

notes.name: Iterative Table-Based Exponential
notes.description: A digit-recurrence family: two small tables per step drive L_i toward zero, cancelling alpha_i-1 leading bits so the datapath narrows monotonically, then rectangular multipliers reconstruct — cumulated multiplier area is about one full multiplier, and it suits LUT-only fabrics and ASIC, not DSP/BRAM FPGAs.
source_headings: Iterative computation of $e^Y$ using small tables and rectangular multipliers

notes.name: Direct eY Table
notes.description: A single ROM addressed by the whole reduced argument Y — no arithmetic at all, and the only eY evaluator that is correctly rounded; costs 2^(wF+g) entries, so it dies above about 8 fraction bits.

notes.name: eA Table
notes.description: The 2^k-entry ROM holding e^A, with the half-ulp rounding bit pre-added to every entry so the final round-by-truncation is free, and a truncated output T_trunc sized to balance the multiplier.
source_headings: ## Using large tables and square multipliers

notes.name: hZ Table
notes.description: A small correctly-rounded ROM for h(Z) = e^Z - Z - 1, whose MSB sits at -2k-1 so the table is 2k bits narrower than e^Z; 2^8 x 6 bits for IEEE single, and it needs only the top bits of Z.
source_headings: ## Using large tables and square multipliers

notes.name: Polynomial hZ Evaluator
notes.description: Replaces the h(Z) ROM with the generic piecewise-polynomial evaluator on h(x) = e^(2^-k x) - 2^-k x - 1, giving two independent knobs (k for the eA table, d for the polynomial's table-vs-multiplier split) and scaling to double precision at k=9, d=2.

notes.name: Higher-Order eY Architecture
notes.description: eA table, h(Z) evaluator, F = Z + H adder, a near-square truncated multiplier T_trunc x F, and a final add-and-truncate — the workhorse eY datapath from single precision upward, landing under 5u of architectural error.
source_headings: ## Using large tables and square multipliers

notes.name: First-Order eY Architecture
notes.description: Drops the h box entirely by taking f(Z) ~ Z: eA table, one multiplier T_trunc x Z, one adder, truncate. Cheapest eY for binary16 (6x8 multiplier, 2 Kbit table) but the eA table grows as 2^(wF/2) and kills it by single precision.

notes.name: eY DSP and BRAM Mapping
notes.description: The single-precision case study: both tables packed into one 36 Kbit dual-port BRAM as 2^10 x 36, one 18x18 DSP whose product is therefore exact and can be rounded to nearest — killing the multiplier error term for one extra bit of final adder.

notes.name: eY Iterative Reduction Step
notes.description: One step of L_{i+1} = L_i - L_i^dagger: the alpha_i leading bits of L_i address two ROMs (X_i^dagger and L_i^dagger = ln E_i^dagger), and the subtraction cancels alpha_i - 1 MSBs so the datapath narrows monotonically toward L_n ~ 0.
source_headings: ## Iterative computation of $e^Y$ using small tables and rectangular multipliers

notes.name: eY Iterative Reconstruction Step
notes.description: One step of X_i = X_{i+1} * X_i^dagger + X_{i+1} + X_i^dagger run with decreasing i: a rectangular w x alpha_i multiplier plus an adder, with the leading one never stored, and all n multipliers cumulating to barely more than one full multiplier.
source_headings: ## Iterative computation of $e^Y$ using small tables and rectangular multipliers

notes.name: Tapped Delay Line
notes.description: Shift register whose every stage is broken out as a tap; the memory that separates a filter from a stateless function evaluator, at one register per sample of history.
source_headings: ### Specifying LTI filters by constant-coefficient equations

notes.name: Direct-Form FIR Filter
notes.description: Register chain feeding one constant multiplier per tap into an adder chain; the literal transcription of a convolution, at n+1 multipliers all fed by the narrow input word.
source_headings: ### Specifying LTI filters by constant-coefficient equations

notes.name: Transposed Direct-Form FIR Filter
notes.description: Reverse every wire of the direct form: one multiple-constant multiplication of u(k) followed by delays and structural adders, cutting the critical path to one multiplier plus one adder at the cost of wider registers.
source_headings: ### Specifying LTI filters by constant-coefficient equations

notes.name: Direct Form I IIR Filter
notes.description: One SOPC over both the input and the fed-back output history; the cheapest multipliers of any IIR form because the b_i see the narrow input, paid for with two unshared delay lines.
source_headings: ### Specifying LTI filters by constant-coefficient equations
### Overall error analysis of a direct-form implementation

notes.name: Transposed Direct Form I IIR Filter
notes.description: Direct form I with every wire reversed, so its building block is an MCM rather than an SOPC; same delay count, shorter adder chain, different rounding behaviour.
source_headings: ### Specifying LTI filters by constant-coefficient equations

notes.name: Direct Form II IIR Filter
notes.description: Commute the recursive and non-recursive halves so both delay lines hold the same values and can be shared, halving registers — but the b_i now multiply the loop signal t'(k) and must be built at extended precision.
source_headings: ### Specifying LTI filters by constant-coefficient equations
### Abstract filter structures versus finite-precision circuits

notes.name: Transposed Direct Form II IIR Filter
notes.description: Shares registers like DF-II yet multiplies the b_i by the narrow u(k) like DF-I — the best area at equal guaranteed accuracy, at a critical path of two multipliers and two adders.
source_headings: ### Specifying LTI filters by constant-coefficient equations
### Abstract filter structures versus finite-precision circuits

notes.name: SOPC, Sum of Products by Constants
notes.description: The whole filter body as one bit heap — every partial product a shifted copy of an input word, compressed once and rounded once — which is what makes the internal guard bits cheap to buy.
source_headings: ### Overall error analysis of a direct-form implementation

notes.name: Biquad Section
notes.description: Second-order IIR section whose two coefficients follow directly from a resonance frequency and a 60 dB decay time; the numerically best-conditioned unit from which larger filters are assembled.
source_headings: ### Filters defined by their coefficients, and filters defined in the frequency domain

notes.name: Biquad Cascade
notes.description: Factor the transfer function into second-order sections chained in series; each section's poles are conditioned independently, so coefficient quantisation cannot drag a whole high-order denominator outside the unit circle.
source_headings: ### Discrete-time signals, elementary operations, systems, LTI filters
### Filter design as an optimisation problem

notes.name: Additive Synthesis Filter Bank
notes.description: Parallel bank of biquads, each a decaying harmonic, gain-scaled and summed; legal because convolution distributes over addition, and it turns a physical bell model into hardware with per-mode WCPGs near 2e5.
source_headings: ### Filters defined by their coefficients, and filters defined in the frequency domain

notes.name: Linear-Phase FIR Filter
notes.description: Symmetric (or antisymmetric) coefficients let taps be pre-added in pairs, halving the multiplications and making the zero-phase response real-valued — the property that lets a frequency mask enter a linear program at all.
source_headings: ### Frequency constraints for linear-phase FIR filters in ILP

notes.name: Minimum-Adder FIR Filter
notes.description: The adder graph an ILP returns when the frequency mask, the coefficient quantisation and the shift-and-add sharing are one problem: 23 adders instead of 37 for the same low-pass spec.
source_headings: ### Frequency constraints for linear-phase FIR filters in ILP

notes.name: Quantized MAC Neuron
notes.description: The integer sum-of-products datapath of one artificial neuron: exact p=m+n products into a q-bit accumulator so the layer is bit-exact against a binary32 simulation of the same 8-bit data — at the cost of an accumulator wider than anything ever stored.

notes.name: Requantization Unit
notes.description: Shift, round, saturate and narrow the wide accumulator back to the layer's output word size, folded into the ReLU that follows it — the single point where all of a DNN layer's error is introduced.

notes.name: ReLU Unit
notes.description: Sign test plus multiplexer: the activation function that costs nothing, kills the vanishing-gradient problem, and whose piecewise linearity is what legalises free choice of scaling factors everywhere else in the datapath.

notes.name: Softmax Unit
notes.description: Exponential per output plus one reciprocal, normalising the output vector to sum to 1 — the most expensive layer in an inference network and the one you are usually allowed to delete.

notes.name: Argmax Unit
notes.description: A comparator tree emitting a one-hot winner: replaces softmax at inference because softmax is monotonic, trading an exponential-and-divide layer for log N comparator levels.

notes.name: Max Pooling Unit
notes.description: A comparator tree over a 2x2 strided window, halving width and height per channel for the cost of three comparators and no arithmetic at all.

notes.name: Average Pooling Unit
notes.description: A four-input adder tree and a two-bit right shift per window — exact, cheaper than a comparator tree in LUTs, and the variant modern CNNs mostly abandoned.

notes.name: Convolution Line Buffer
notes.description: Two row FIFOs and nine registers presenting a fresh 3x3 window every cycle to a dedicated sum-of-products — the canonical building block of a stream/dataflow CNN, buying one activation per clock for two rows of storage.

notes.name: Winograd Convolution
notes.description: Pre-addition, element-wise multiply, post-addition: computes m outputs of an r-tap convolution in the provably minimal m+r-1 multiplications, and stops paying once the multiplier is small enough that three adders cost more than one multiply.

notes.name: TPU
notes.description: A 256x256 systolic array of int8 MAC cells with weights resident and 32-bit 256-deep accumulators — the generic end of the DNN accelerator spectrum, where 16-bit operands are emulated in time at half or quarter throughput.

notes.name: XNOR-Popcount Neuron
notes.description: Encode -1 as 0 and the multiplier becomes one XNOR gate, the adder tree becomes a population counter, and the activation plus folded batch norm becomes a single unsigned threshold comparator — a neuron with no arithmetic operator left in it.

notes.name: Ternary MAC Unit
notes.description: Weights restricted to -1, 0, +1 turn every multiply-accumulate into an add, a subtract, or nothing at all — zero weights delete hardware outright, which is what makes an unrolled million-MAC CNN fit an FPGA.

notes.name: Digit-Serial Adder
notes.description: One digit of the sum per cycle with the carry held in a register: radix-16 for four cycles per 16-bit word, radix-2 for sixteen — how you spend the slack after pooling cuts the data rate to a quarter and then a sixteenth.

notes.name: LogicNet Neuron
notes.description: The entire neuron — constant products, accumulation, batch norm and activation — tabulated into one LUT6, so its cost depends only on input and output word size and never on what it computes.

notes.name: LNS Neuron
notes.description: Log-domain weights and activations: the multiply is an adder, an antilog table returns to fixed point for an exact sum, and one log(ReLU1) table closes the loop — good accuracy at 4 to 6 bits, at which point both tables are plain FPGA LUTs.

notes.name: Log-Activation Shift Neuron
notes.description: Keep weights linear and activations logarithmic and the multiplier degenerates to a barrel shifter, with a leading-one detector re-encoding the ReLU output back into the log domain.

notes.name: Virtual-Channel Router
notes.description: The whole per-tile switch as a 4-stage pipeline (RC/VA/SA/ST) — buys segmented links and local arbitration instead of a die-spanning bus, at the cost of one router and ~H hops of latency per tile.

notes.name: Dimension-Order Routing Unit
notes.description: Two magnitude comparators feeding a 5-way priority mux that emits E/W/N/S/L — stateless deadlock-free routing for a mesh, at the cost of zero path diversity.
source_headings: Worked example: a 4-flit packet under XY and wormhole

notes.name: Turn Model Routing
notes.description: Routing logic that forbids exactly one turn per abstract cycle (west-first / north-last / negative-first) — buys back partial adaptivity that XY throws away, at the cost of a productive-set encoder plus a runtime selection function.

notes.name: Dateline Virtual Channel Allocation
notes.description: Splits every physical torus link into VC0/VC1 with a one-bit header field flipped at a fixed dateline — cuts the wraparound cycle so a torus routes deadlock-free, at 2x the input buffers and a 2:1 mux per link.
source_headings: Quality of service and virtual channels

notes.name: Virtual Channel Buffer
notes.description: V independent flit queues sharing one physical input port — gives the switch arbiter V independent heads, lifting the 2-sqrt(2) head-of-line saturation bound toward 1 at a linear V*B*w buffer cost.
source_headings: Quality of service and virtual channels

notes.name: Crossbar Switch
notes.description: p independent p:1 muxes replicated w times — any-input-to-any-output in one cycle, at p^2*w crosspoints, the term that makes high radix quadratically expensive.

notes.name: Fixed-Priority Arbiter
notes.description: Grants the lowest set request via g = r AND (-r), reassociated as a prefix-OR so depth falls from n to log2(n) — cheapest possible grant, at the cost of unbounded starvation.

notes.name: Round-Robin Arbiter
notes.description: Two prefix trees, an n-bit mux and a pointer register: masked priority encode with fallback — fair, starvation-free grants, and usually the circuit that sets the router's clock period.

notes.name: Separable Input-First Allocator
notes.description: p input arbiters of V:1 followed by p output arbiters of p:1 — switch allocation in O(log V + log p) delay, accepting a worse matching than a full allocator.

notes.name: Wavefront Allocator
notes.description: A pV x p priority-wave matching array that finds a maximal matching in one pass — better crossbar utilisation than separable allocation, at a longer combinational wave through the array.

notes.name: Credit-Based Flow Control
notes.description: An up/down mirror counter of ceil(log2(B+1)) bits per output VC, send gated on count>0 — lossless backpressure with full link utilisation whenever B >= t_crt.
source_headings: Worked example: a 4-flit packet under XY and wormhole

notes.name: Store-and-Forward Flow Control
notes.description: Allocates buffer and channel per packet and forwards nothing until the tail lands — trivial control, at H*(t_r+L) latency and B >= L buffering.

notes.name: Virtual Cut-Through Flow Control
notes.description: Forwards the head as soon as the downstream can hold the whole packet — pays serialization once, H*t_r+(L-1), but still needs B >= L so a blocked packet collapses into one node.

notes.name: Wormhole Flow Control
notes.description: Channel allocated per packet, buffers per flit — decouples buffer depth from packet length entirely, at the cost of a stalled worm holding channels across several routers.
source_headings: Worked example: a 4-flit packet under XY and wormhole

notes.name: Lookahead Routing
notes.description: Computes hop i+1's output port during hop i and carries it in the head flit — removes route computation from the critical path for one extra port field per flit.

notes.name: Speculative Switch Allocation
notes.description: Runs switch allocation in parallel with VC allocation and squashes the grant on VA failure — buys a whole pipeline stage for a small misspeculation rate.

notes.name: Mesochronous Link FIFO
notes.description: A 2-4 flit phase-tolerant buffer with a strobe trained once at reset — crosses a constant-phase clock boundary with no synchronizer latency, freeing the design from a global skew budget.

notes.name: Dual-Clock Asynchronous FIFO
notes.description: Gray-coded write/read pointers cross-sampled through two-flop synchronizers — safe full/empty across unrelated clocks because one bit changes per increment, at 2-3 cycles of added credit round-trip.

notes.name: Bundled-Data Handshake Link
notes.description: Four-phase req/ack sequencing with a Muller C-element join and a matched delay line — clockless link traversal with data-dependent latency, at the price of a timing assumption STA cannot check.
notes.spade_note: The C-element join is combinational feedback (y+ = ab + y(a+b)); Spade has no latch primitive and `let` cannot self-reference, and the link has no clock to register on.

notes.name: TDM Slot Table Scheduler
notes.description: An offline-computed (slot, input) -> output table cycled by a modulo-S counter — a hard latency bound of (S-1)+H and exact n/S bandwidth, paid for by wasted idle reservations.
source_headings: Quality of service and virtual channels

notes.name: Priority Aging Arbiter
notes.description: A saturating wait counter per VC added to the class priority before comparison — bounds starvation under fixed-priority QoS, at log2(P_max) bits per VC and a wider arbiter compare.
source_headings: Quality of service and virtual channels

notes.name: Deficit Round Robin Scheduler
notes.description: Per-VC quantum accumulator that transmits while the deficit covers a flit — weighted fair sharing to within one flit with one adder and one comparator per VC.
source_headings: Quality of service and virtual channels

notes.name: Frequency-Directed Pipelining
notes.description: Inverts the usual flow: you state f, the tool solves for N. Splitting a combinatorial DAG into N stages of delay dt/N multiplies throughput by N at the cost of the registers between them.
source_headings: ### Automatic pipelining, the user point of view

notes.name: Pipeline Synchronization Delay Line
notes.description: The hardware the scheduler actually emits: a per-signal shift register sized by the cycle gap, so reconverging paths of a DAG meet in the same stage — effSub_d3 is effSub through three registers.
source_headings: ### Automatic pipelining, the user point of view

notes.name: Register Sandwich
notes.description: Wraps the preceding operator in input and output registers so the backend measures a real register-to-register f_max instead of an unbounded combinatorial path.
source_headings: ### Automatic pipelining, the user point of view

notes.name: Pipelined Floating-Point Adder
notes.description: The canonical worked case: the FPAdd datapath cut by three synchronization barriers into four stages, with the shifter, LZC and rounding adder each landing in a different one.

notes.name: Shared Bit Heap
notes.description: Several multipliers throw bits onto one common heap and do no local compression, so a sum of products costs exactly one compressor tree — the multipliers stop being VHDL entities at all.

notes.name: Trailing Zero Counter
notes.description: Monotone thermometer chain of two-input ANDs whose population count is the trailing-zero count; linear in word size instead of the quadratic naive wide-AND encoding, and the objective row for coefficient-wordlength minimization.

notes.name: Minimal-Adder Adder Graph
notes.description: The shift/add/subtract DAG an ILP feasibility solve returns for a single constant, e.g. 93X in two adders against three for CSD; proven minimal, but only up to ~20-bit constants before the run-time wall.

folded.spade_note: An axiom system, not a structure.

folded.name: De Morgan's Laws
folded.description: Complementing a function complements every literal and swaps every operator; the law behind bubble pushing, NAND-only design and the two's-complement identity.
folded.spade_note: An identity, not a structure; its hardware consequence is the NAND-NAND Network.

folded.name: Consensus Theorem
folded.description: The consensus term is logically redundant but hazard-suppressing: keeping it is how a two-level cover becomes static-hazard-free.

folded.name: Functional Completeness
folded.description: NAND alone and NOR alone generate every Boolean function; the only two single-operator complete sets among the sixteen binary functions.

folded.name: Literal Count and Logic Depth
folded.description: The two cost metrics every later trade-off is quoted in: 2L transistors for area, gate levels for delay, honest only under bounded fan-in.
folded.spade_note: Definitions of cost measures, no structure of their own.

folded.name: Propagation and Contamination Delay
folded.description: t_pd is the longest sensitised path and bounds the clock through setup; t_cd is the shortest and must be big enough for hold — a block that is too fast is a violation you cannot slow the clock to fix.
folded.spade_note: Timing definitions and static-timing bookkeeping; no circuit of its own, the RTL lives in the blocks being timed.
source_headings: ## Propagation delay, contamination delay, and the critical path

folded.name: Metastability and MTBF
folded.description: Cut the master latch off mid-regeneration and it sits near the unstable point, diverging as exp(t/tau) with no bounded resolution time — giving an MTBF linear in everything but the exponent.
folded.spade_note: An analog small-signal failure mode of the bistable, with a probabilistic model. No synthesizable structure; the circuit that answers it is the Synchronizer Chain note.

folded.name: Time Borrowing
folded.description: The arrival-time recurrence A_{i+1} = max(t_i, A_i) + D_{i+1} and the window constraint it collapses to: the running average over every run of length L, not the worst stage, sets the clock — bounded by a single B, not L*B.
folded.spade_note: Timing analysis, not a structure: the recurrence and its unrolled inequality family describe a constraint on the pipeline, not hardware.

folded.name: Latch Race-Through
folded.description: The min-delay constraint delta_dq + delta_{i+1} >= t_h + t_sk - t_nov: T does not appear, so slowing the clock cannot fix it, but widening the non-overlap gap can drive the requirement negative — free hold margin, paid for out of B.
folded.spade_note: A min-delay inequality on an existing pipeline, not a distinct structure.

folded.name: Latch Loop Timing Analysis
folded.description: Why a cyclic latch graph forces arrival times to a fixed-point iteration: PrimeTime and OpenSTA iterate till converge at up to O(n^2) with no divergent-loop lookahead, and cycle-cutting trades that runtime for silent pessimism.
folded.spade_note: An STA engine algorithm, not a circuit.
source_headings: EDA tool support — the real answer

folded.name: Flip-Flop to Latch Conversion
folded.description: The synthesis transform: two-colour the latch graph, split each flop into an L1/L2 pair separated by retimed logic, and pin a latch at every original flop position so combinational LEC still finds matching state points.
folded.spade_note: A netlist transform run by a tool — graph two-colouring plus retiming — with no RTL of its own.
source_headings: EDA tool support — the real answer

folded.name: Synchronous Discipline
folded.description: Every signal-flow cycle passes one edge-triggered flop on one clock, so combinational glitching costs nothing and correctness collapses to one setup inequality per path.

folded.name: State Minimization
folded.description: Moore-Hopcroft partition refinement merges states no input sequence can distinguish; it shrinks flop count, not necessarily gate count, and the output column it starts from is the whole Moore-vs-Mealy state difference.
folded.spade_note: Design-time partition-refinement algorithm run on the state table, not a structure that is instantiated; the minimised machine it produces is the RTL of the Moore Machine and Mealy Machine notes.

folded.name: Primitive Flow Table
folded.description: Writes the spec down as one stable state per row, then merges rows through a merger diagram and a closed cover — the async replacement for state minimisation, and the closure check everyone forgets.
folded.spade_note: A specification artefact plus a maximal-clique/closed-cover search — a solver algorithm, not a structure. The circuit it produces is the Huffman Feedback Model note.

folded.name: Essential Hazard
folded.description: A fault of the table, not the cover: one input change can be overtaken by a state change and land where three changes would — the only cure is a deliberate delay in the feedback path.
folded.spade_note: Unger's three-change test applies to a fundamental-mode feedback machine, and the repair is a physical delay element. Neither has a Spade form; the clocked flip-flop that hides the hazard inside a cell is the nearest native structure.

folded.name: Quasi-Delay-Insensitive Circuits
folded.description: Pure delay-insensitivity can compute almost nothing, so QDI buys the design space back with one repair — the isochronic fork — and that single assumption is the whole timing closure.
folded.spade_note: A hierarchy of timing models and an assumption about wire forks; no structure of its own. The circuits it governs are the C-element and Muller pipeline notes.

folded.name: Unsigned Fixed-Point Format
folded.description: Names a format by two bit positions instead of two bit counts, so ulp, range and width all fall out of arithmetic on m and l — and the scale factor 2^l costs no hardware.

folded.name: Sign-Magnitude Format
folded.description: A symmetric range and a trivial sign flip, paid for with two zeros, a broken equality test and separate add/subtract datapaths — which is why it survives only inside floating-point significands.
source_headings: ### Two's complement as an algebraic object

folded.name: High-Radix Digit Grouping
folded.description: Chunking w bits into k digits of alpha bits costs zero logic and is the standard lever for trading iteration count against per-iteration complexity.

folded.name: Signed-Digit Number System
folded.description: Allowing more digits than the radix makes representations non-unique, which is exactly the freedom that lets a digit absorb an incoming carry instead of propagating it.

folded.name: Subnormal Encoding
folded.description: Drops the implicit bit and freezes the exponent to fill the gap around zero, buying the property x-y=0 iff x=y — and costing every operator a dedicated shifter, a leading-zero counter and a MUX.
source_headings: ### Nfloat: the simplification for application-specific hardware

folded.name: Biased Exponent Encoding
folded.description: Adding E0 = 2^(wE-1)-1 instead of using two's complement makes the bit pattern of a positive float monotone in its value, so a float comparator is an integer comparator and "next float" is an increment.

folded.name: Minifloat Formats
folded.description: The same (wE, wF) machinery redistributed for machine learning — bfloat16 keeps binary32's range so conversion is a truncation, TF32 serves both binary16 and binary32, and FP8 E4M3 trades infinities for a binade.

folded.name: Logarithmic Number System
folded.description: Store the fractional exponent instead of the significand: relative resolution is exactly uniform, no binade transitions, and zero has to be pushed into an exception field because log 0 is -infinity.

folded.name: Absolute and Relative Error
folded.description: Fixes what an operator's error even is: a function of X, quoted as its worst case, absolute for fixed point and relative for floating point.
folded.spade_note: Definitions 3.1-3.2 are mathematical; there is no hardware in section 3.1.1.

folded.name: Unit in the Last Place
folded.description: The quantum of a format, constant in fixed point and per-binade in floating point — the unit that lets an accuracy spec be stated without naming the format.

folded.name: Parametric Operator Design
folded.description: Refuse every architectural design choice by promoting it to an internal parameter, so the generator produces a search space instead of one point.

folded.name: Table Maker's Dilemma
folded.description: Why correct rounding is mandated for +,-,x,/,sqrt and nothing else: without a hardest-to-round bound, no number of guard bits can decide the final rounding.
folded.spade_note: A decidability result about function evaluation, not a circuit.
source_headings: ## Rounding to the Nearest When an Approximation Is Involved

folded.name: FPGA Fabric
folded.description: The substrate every cost in this vault is billed against: an array of logic elements in a switch-matrix interconnect, configured from SRAM after manufacture — and the routing is the bulk of the area.
folded.spade_note: The fabric is the target of compilation, not a synthesizable block: routing, switch matrices, connection blocks and I/O have no RTL description.

folded.name: FPGA-ASIC Performance Gap
folded.description: An FPGA runs the same circuit about 10x slower than silicon, and the cause is the reconfigurable routing — three things buy the gap back: no program management, exact parallelism, bit-level granularity.
folded.spade_note: An architectural argument comparing substrates; there is no circuit to compile.

folded.name: Operator Fusion vs Resource Sharing
folded.description: Merging every heap in an operator into one buys depth and area, but only until a shared sub-result has to be recomputed — the fixed-point sine/cosine datapath is where the two techniques collide.
folded.spade_note: A design-space trade-off between two architectural strategies, not a structure; the concrete datapath it argues over is owned by the CORDIC and polynomial hubs.
source_headings: ### From Bit Arrays to Bit Heaps
### Bit Heaps as the Portable Substrate

folded.name: Constant Bit Merging
folded.description: Every synthesis-time constant in a heap — truncation half-ulps, the round-to-nearest bit, sign-extension ones, subtraction's LSB one — precomputes into at most one constant bit per column, which is why round-to-nearest usually costs nothing.
source_headings: ## Expressing a Computation as a Bit Heap

folded.name: Algebraic Dot Transformations
folded.description: Six identities (2x, 3x, x+1, y+xy, x+x̄, x^k=x) that shorten columns before any hardware is picked, each reversible, and each turning a computed bit into a shifted or constant one.

folded.name: ILP-Based Compressor Tree Synthesis
folded.description: Models compression as min Σ c_e·k_(s,e,c) under four constraints — every bit consumed, produced bits propagated, output height capped at I=2 or 3, row compressors split into low/middle/high parts — with the stage count held constant and swept upward; optimal, but limited to a few hundred bits at a 1-hour Gurobi timeout.
folded.spade_note: A MILP model and solver flow, not a structure; the compressed tree it returns is written up in the sibling heuristic and tree notes.

folded.name: Multiplier Tiling ILP
folded.description: Binary ILP that returns the provably minimum-cost tiling: one placement variable per (tile, position), one equality constraint per rectangle position, plus a DSP budget constraint to sweep the LUT/DSP trade-off.
folded.spade_note: A binary integer-linear-programming model solved offline by a generator; the circuit it emits is the note Multiplier Tiling.

folded.name: Optimally Truncated Multiplier Tiling
folded.description: Lets the ILP itself choose which rectangle positions stay uncovered, bounding |C - delta_tiling| below one half-ulp, so efficient 2xk tiles replace the wasteful 1x1s of the guard-bit shape.
folded.spade_note: An extended ILP model (constraints C1-C4 plus the bit decomposition of the compensation constant); the hardware it emits is a tiled truncated multiplier.
source_headings: ### Optimal tiling for truncated multipliers on FPGAs

folded.name: Multiplier Error Propagation
folded.description: An exact multiplier still amplifies its inputs' errors; balancing the three surviving terms gives l_P ≈ m_Y + l_X ≈ m_X + l_Y, hence w_X ≈ w_Y — why truncated square multipliers are the sweet spot.
folded.spade_note: A parametric error analysis plus the format/MSB specification rules that follow from it; no hardware of its own.

folded.name: P-D Diagram
folded.description: The plane of (D, beta*R_i) sliced into overlapping selection wedges — the construction that says how coarsely you may truncate D and the remainder before a fixed-size selection table stops existing.
folded.spade_note: A plot and an inequality argument (9.28)-(9.30), not a structure; the hardware it justifies lives in Quotient Digit Selection Table.
source_headings: ## Redundant Digit Sets and the Selection-Interval Overlap

folded.name: SCM ILP Model
folded.description: Recasts "cheapest adder graph for C" as an integer program, buying retargetability to power, fan-out, depth or full-adder count at the price of a solver run.
folded.spade_note: A solver formulation, not a structure; the circuit it returns is Minimum-Adder Constant Multiplier.

folded.name: Magic Constant Exactness Condition
folded.description: Why p >= w + r is required for reciprocal multiplication to be exact: the pre-floor value already carries R/D, so the error budget is 1/D ulp, not 1 ulp.
folded.spade_note: A constraint on the compile-time choice of (A, B, p), not hardware — the circuit it governs is Recip Constant Divider.
source_headings: > [!important] This is a *stronger* requirement than faithful rounding

folded.name: Divisor Factorisation Search
folded.description: Choosing which factorisation of D to build and in what order: the inequality 1/(a-ra) + 1/(a-rb) < 1/(a-rD), and why the small factor goes first.
folded.spade_note: A compile-time cost-model search over factorisations; the hardware it selects is the Composite Constant Divider.
source_headings: ### When two small tables beat one large one

folded.name: Integer Power Output Format
folded.description: Fixes the exact output format of X^p from the input format: LSB is always p*l, and for signed X the parity of p decides whether the result is ufix or sfix.
folded.spade_note: A format derivation, not hardware — it sizes the wires of every other circuit in this hub but synthesises to nothing on its own.

folded.name: Constant Truncation for Correct Rounding
folded.description: How many bits k of an irrational constant guarantee correct rounding: the minimum distance to a midpoint sets k ~ 2w_F+1, for under 2x the area.
folded.spade_note: Compile-time search — exhaustive enumeration of F_X in 512-bit arithmetic, or continued fractions. No hardware; the resulting multiplier is the Correctly Rounded Floating-Point Constant Multiplier note.
source_headings: ### Correctly rounded multiplication by a real constant

folded.name: Unsafe Floating-Point Rewrites
folded.description: Which algebraic simplifications an HLS compiler may not make, and why signed zeros, infinities and NaN break x/x, x-x, 0*x and x+0.
folded.spade_note: C-standard semantics and compiler policy — a table of non-equivalences, not a structure. The one hardware consequence is catalogued separately as Divide-by-Self Specialization.
source_headings: ## Floating-point optimizations in an HLS context

folded.name: Fixed-Point Range Wrap
folded.description: When RN(f(X)) hits 2^(m+1) the modulo property of fixed point silently returns the smallest value instead of the largest — a corner-case bug that gets rarer, not safer, as precision grows.
folded.spade_note: A failure mode of a format choice, not a structure; the fixes below carry the RTL.
source_headings: ## Worked example — 4-bit sin(pi/2 x), and the trap

folded.name: Faithful Rounding Monotonicity
folded.description: Correct rounding of a monotonic function is monotonic for free; faithful rounding is a relation, not a function, and can wobble — by provably at most one ulp.
folded.spade_note: A property of a rounding relation, proved by composition; no structure of its own.
source_headings: ## Worked example — 4-bit sin(pi/2 x), and the trap

folded.name: Function Domain Normalization
folded.description: Never give a generator interval bounds [a,b]: fold the change of variable into f itself, leaving one Boolean signedIn and the two grid-aligned domains [0,1) and [-1,1).
folded.spade_note: A generator interface decision executed at generation time in Sollya; it emits no gates.

folded.name: LDTC Parameter Search
folded.description: Enumerates (s, w_H, w_L), filters by cost before validity, and proves a vector legal by a per-slice max-min test costing 2^(w_A-s) not 2^w_A.
folded.spade_note: Algorithms 17.1 and 17.2 are an offline software search over table contents; the hardware they emit is the LDTC note.
source_headings: ### The optimization algorithm and validity test

folded.name: Multipartite Guard-Bit Budget
folded.description: Splits one ulp three ways — final rounding, m+1 table fills, approximation — and solves for the number g of guard bits, rejecting a decomposition outright when the approximation error alone exceeds half an ulp.
folded.spade_note: Pure error analysis: the balanced-chord-slope derivation and the closed form for g. The hardware it sizes lives in Multipartite Methods.
source_headings: ### Error analysis: splitting one ulp three ways
### Computing the sizes of the sub-tables

folded.name: Multipartite Decomposition Search
folded.description: Enumerates all decompositions {alpha, beta, m, (gamma_i, p_i, beta_i)}, pruned by gamma_min and a precomputed 24^3 error array, finding a 16-bit sine 70x smaller than the plain table in under a second.
folded.spade_note: Algorithm 17.3 is a FloPoCo-side generator, not a datapath.

folded.name: Machine-Efficient Coefficient Quantization
folded.description: Searches directly over polynomials with representable coefficients, so coefficient rounding disappears from the error budget instead of adding a term.
folded.spade_note: Algorithm 18.1 is a generate-time search loop calling Sollya fpminimax/supnorm; it emits table contents, not a datapath.

folded.name: Polynomial Evaluator Error Budget
folded.description: Splits one ulp three ways — free final rounding, approximation, evaluation — and hands the leftover slack to the datapath sizing; the equation that joins the chapter's three halves.
folded.spade_note: A budget equation (18.33-18.36) consumed by the generator. The free final rounding it describes is a wire truncation plus a half-ulp pre-added into C0, catalogued under [[Rounding]].

folded.name: Polynomial Approximator Generator Flow
folded.description: The two FloPoCo pipelines — FixFunctionBySimplePoly and FixFunctionByPiecewisePoly — that turn (f, lsbIn, lsbOut, d) into sized VHDL, and the extremal-subinterval trick that makes the alpha search fast.
folded.spade_note: Software generator flow (Figs. 18.22-18.23); its output is the RTL of the other notes in this hub.

folded.name: Rational Fraction Approximation
folded.description: Degree (n,m) buys roughly the accuracy of degree n+m — the same multipliers plus a divider, which is why the book declines it outside the E-method.
folded.spade_note: The chapter gives no architecture for it: Sect. 18.1.7 is a definition (18.2) plus a verdict. The one hardware form, the E-method, lives in Chap. 19.
source_headings: ## Polynomials Are a Special Case of Rational Fractions

folded.name: Simple E-Fractions
folded.description: The coefficient-search problem deciding whether the E-method applies at all: |Q_i|+|x|<mu and |P_i|<zeta after power-of-two scaling, which most minimax rational fits fail.
folded.spade_note: An offline coefficient search over machine-representable P_i and Q_i (Brisebarre et al. 2018), not a datapath; the resulting coefficients are wired into the E-Method note.
source_headings: ### Rational approximations compatible with the E-method

folded.name: Binary Angle Representation
folded.description: Angles as sfix(0,l) fractions of pi, so modulo-2pi periodicity becomes the free modulo-2 wrap of two's complement and any wider argument costs nothing to reduce.
folded.spade_note: A number-format definition plus the scaled-output choice f=(1-2^l)sin(pi x); the only hardware is dropping integer bits, i.e. wiring. The DDS phase accumulator it enables is a register+adder that belongs to a different hub.

folded.name: CORDIC Scale Factor Compensation
folded.description: Dropping cos(alpha_i) makes each step multiplier-free but grows the modulus by a data-independent K; initialising at 1/K cancels it for free, and the output scaling rides along.
folded.spade_note: K = prod sqrt(1+2^-2i) is a compile-time constant folded into the hardwired initial C1 together with (1-2^l); it instantiates no hardware of its own. Borderline - if the note ends up showing an explicit shift-add compensator it should be reclassified verified.

folded.name: CORDIC Error Budget
folded.description: One inequality sizes the whole operator: half an ulp to final rounding, a quarter to stopping the iteration (n = -l+2), a quarter to compounding truncations (g from the recurrence).
folded.spade_note: A design procedure - a software-evaluated error recurrence (20.39) that returns the integers n and g. The truncate-vs-round-to-nearest verdict it produces is realised in CORDIC Rotation Mode, not here.
source_headings: ### Approximation error and the number of iterations

folded.name: Exact Accumulation Reproducibility
folded.description: Why an exact accumulator is order-independent — the summands are integers and two's complement is a ring — and why that still does not make the application accurate.
folded.spade_note: A ring-homomorphism argument about why the accumulator's result is order-independent, plus the book's fallacy box. No hardware of its own; every circuit it justifies is catalogued separately.

folded.name: Exponential Guard-Bit Budget
folded.description: The derivation that fixes g=3: half the 1-ulp target is eaten by the final rounding alone, the M<1 branch doubles both remaining terms, and an XOR-only negate costs a whole extra guard bit across the datapath to save one carry chain.
folded.spade_note: A closed-form error budget and a parameter derivation, not a structure — it dimensions every other note in this hub but synthesizes to nothing itself.

folded.name: eY Additive Argument Split
folded.description: Splits Y by bit position into A (k MSBs) and Z (the rest) so e^Y = e^A * e^Z, then rewrites it as e^A + e^A*f(Z) with f = Z + h(Z) — pure wiring and two algebraic moves that shrink the multiplier by k bits and the function evaluator by 2k bits.
source_headings: ## Using large tables and square multipliers

folded.name: eY Error Budget
folded.description: The telescoping decomposition of delta_arch into seven terms (final round, multiplier, T truncation, h evaluator, Z truncation, an exactly-zero term, table) and how the resulting 3u-to-6u total sets the guard-bit split between g and g'.
folded.spade_note: A pen-and-paper error decomposition that fixes the parameters t, p, k, g, g'; no hardware of its own — the hardware it constrains is the Higher-Order and First-Order eY architectures.

folded.name: Worst-Case Peak Gain
folded.description: The single number sum|h(k)| that turns BIBO stability into arithmetic: it sizes the output MSB, and its defining adversarial input is constructible as a test-bench signal.
folded.spade_note: A mathematical quantity computed at design time by an arbitrary-precision software library (FloPoCo's WCPG); no hardware block corresponds to it. The worst-case exciting signal it induces is a test-bench generator, not a shipped circuit.

folded.name: IIR Guard-Bit Sizing
folded.description: Deleting the numerator of H leaves the filter that amplifies rounding errors; its WCPG says how many LSB guard bits the internal datapath needs — 22 of them for a second-order bell resonator.
folded.spade_note: A sizing formula, l_ext = l' - 1 - ceil(log2 WCPG(H_delta)). H_delta is an analysis artifact that is never built; the circuits it sizes are the direct-form notes.
source_headings: ### Error amplification in the feedback loop
### Overall error analysis of a direct-form implementation

folded.name: Faithful Hardware Digital Filter
folded.description: A hardware filter has no transfer function and no poles, so the frequency question is ill-posed; replace it with a one-ulp bound against an ideal LTI filter and stability, bounded limit cycles and comparability all follow.
folded.spade_note: A definition (Def. 23.3 / 23.6) plus the L-vs-C set argument. The circuits that satisfy it are the direct-form notes.
source_headings: ## An arithmetic approach to the implementation of LTI filters
## Hardware digital filters faithful to an LTI filter
### Discrete-time signals, elementary operations, systems, LTI filters

folded.name: FixIIR Generator
folded.description: Generator interface that takes only real coefficients, an input LSB and an output LSB and derives everything else — internal format, guard bits, test bench — so no user ever picks a width and simulates to check it.
folded.spade_note: A software architecture generator producing VHDL; the interface itself is not a circuit.
source_headings: ### Filter design: from a frequency specification to a time-domain architecture

folded.name: Batch Normalization Folding
folded.description: At inference the batch statistics are constants, so the whole normalisation collapses into the preceding layer's weights and bias: the cleanest constant-fold in the chapter, and the reason no batch-norm hardware exists in an inference datapath.
folded.spade_note: A compile-time weight transformation, not hardware — the whole point is that it produces zero gates. The training-time version is a batch-statistics accumulator the book gives no architecture for.

folded.name: Straight-Through Estimator
folded.description: Quantize on the forward path, keep full-precision weights on the backward path: the trick that lets backpropagation see through a step function with zero gradient, and the reason 5-bit weights reach binary32 accuracy.
folded.spade_note: A training-graph construct. The forward quantizer is the Requantization Unit; the backward identity path exists only in the training software, so there is no separate circuit to compile.

folded.name: Channel Dependency Graph
folded.description: The hold-and-request graph over channels: routing is deadlock-free iff the graph is acyclic — the proof obligation every routing construction discharges by exhibiting a topological order.
folded.spade_note: A graph-theoretic theorem about a routing function, not a circuit; the constructions that satisfy it (XY, turn model, dateline) each have their own note.

folded.name: Interconnect Topology Metrics
folded.description: Diameter, bisection, radix and channel count in closed form for bus/ring/mesh/torus/crossbar/fat tree, and the bound lambda_max = 2*B_B/(N*w) that makes throughput a bisection property, not a diameter one.
folded.spade_note: A counting argument over graphs; no synthesisable structure of its own.

folded.name: Functional and Performance Specification
folded.description: Splits an operator's command line into what it computes (mandatory, no default) and what it costs (optional, defaulted) — the split that makes 'computing just right' mechanically expressible.
folded.spade_note: A parameter taxonomy and tool interface. No structure to compile.
source_headings: ## FloPoCo from a user point of view

folded.name: FloPoCo Operator Class
folded.description: Every generated VHDL entity is an Operator; writing one is writing into a vhdl stream, where declare() registers a signal's name, width and the delay of the op that produced it — and that third argument is the whole timing model.
folded.spade_note: An abstract C++ base class plus a code-emission stream. The circuits it emits are catalogued separately.

folded.name: Target Class Hierarchy
folded.description: One abstract class splits the fabric into architecture facts (lutInputs) and delay facts (logicDelay, adderDelay(n)), so a new chip is a new subclass and never a new operator.
folded.spade_note: A C++ class hierarchy that models fabric parameters. It describes hardware, it is not hardware.

folded.name: Lexicographic Circuit Time
folded.description: Replaces a scalar critical path with the pair (c, tau) — registers crossed, then delay since the last one — ordered lexicographically, so 'later cycle' always dominates 'slower within a cycle'.
folded.spade_note: A timing definition on the dependency graph. It parameterises every other note here but has no structure of its own.
source_headings: ## Worked example: reading a scheduled dependency graph

folded.name: ASAP Pipeline Scheduling
folded.description: Parse the vhdl stream into a labelled dependency graph, schedule every signal as soon as possible, regenerate with delayed signal names — minimal cycle count, but not minimal register count.
folded.spade_note: A graph scheduling heuristic run by the generator at compile time; the circuit it produces is Frequency-Directed Pipelining.
source_headings: ## Worked example: reading a scheduled dependency graph

folded.name: Leiserson-Saxe Retiming
folded.description: The optimal register placement FloPoCo does not do: minimise total register cost subject to a frequency constraint, worth 20-30 percent of the register bill over ASAP.
folded.spade_note: A register-minimisation algorithm on a graph. Its output is the same pipeline structure catalogued under Frequency-Directed Pipelining.
source_headings: ### Automatic pipelining, the user point of view

folded.name: BitHeap Framework
folded.description: The software realization of a sum of weighted bits: columns sorted by arrival time in lexicographic circuit time, an add/subtract interface that sign-extends from the Signal format, and one startCompression() call that emits the whole tree.
folded.spade_note: A C++ data structure and interface; the hardware it emits is the compressor tree owned by hub 2.3.

folded.name: Linear Programming Relaxation
folded.description: Continuous LP whose optimum sits on a polytope vertex and is found in polynomial time by simplex; costs you integrality, so its answer is a bound, not a circuit.
folded.spade_note: Mathematical definition of the LP form (min c^T x s.t. Ax<=b) and the vertex argument. No hardware.

folded.name: Mixed-Integer Linear Program
folded.description: Restricting variables to integers/binaries makes the model exactly express a discrete design space; costs NP-hardness, and the integer optimum is not the rounded LP optimum.
folded.spade_note: Taxonomy (ILP / BILP / MILP) plus the decision-variable idiom. A problem statement, not a circuit.

folded.name: Branch-and-Bound
folded.description: Splits the polytope on a fractional variable and prunes subtrees with the LP bound; buys a proof of optimality, costs a tree that doubles per still-fractional variable.
folded.spade_note: Solver search algorithm. No datapath.
source_headings: ## Addressing the limitations of ILP solvers

folded.name: Boolean Constraint Gadgets
folded.description: Linear inequality systems for NOT, AND, OR, XOR and implication that are the convex hull of the true rows; buys any Boolean relation in an ILP for 1-4 rows and at most one auxiliary variable.
folded.spade_note: The gates themselves are owned by Boolean Algebra; what lives here is their inequality encoding, which is a mathematical definition.

folded.name: Exactly-One Constraint
folded.description: Sum of a binary group equal to one (or at most one), the workhorse for selecting a single architecture alternative; one row, no auxiliary variable, and it is the one-hot select of a mux written as algebra.
folded.spade_note: A selection constraint. Its hardware image, the one-hot multiplexer, is owned by Combinational Logic.

folded.name: Big-M Constraint
folded.description: Turns "X=Y only when z=1" into two linear rows by disabling the constraint with a large M; faster to solve than a native indicator, but the relaxation goes blind at fractional z and 1/M must clear the feasibility tolerance.
folded.spade_note: Constraint-linearization gadget, not a structure.

folded.name: Bit-Split Product Constraint
folded.description: Encodes an integer product Z=X*Y as the shift-and-add sum of big-M-gated partial products; the only route to a variable-times-variable term, at 4w_Y rows, w_Y auxiliary integers, and an M that grows with word size.
folded.spade_note: This is literally the shift-and-add multiplier restated as inequalities; the multiplier RTL is owned by 2.4 Multipliers. Also covers one-hot vs binary integer splitting.
source_headings: ### Splitting integers into their binary representation

folded.name: Integer Feasibility Tolerance
folded.description: The binary64 slack, typically 1e-5 and never below 1e-9, within which a solver calls a value integral; caps the usable dynamic range at about 1e4 and therefore caps big-M, which is why large constants must fall back to native indicators.
folded.spade_note: Solver numerics. No circuit.

folded.name: ScaLP Solver Interface
folded.description: C++ wrapper that dynamically links Gurobi/CPLEX/SCIP/lp_solve from a wishlist and overloads operators onto the algebra; buys solver portability inside FloPoCo, costs you a build whose optimality depends on which solver is installed.
folded.spade_note: Software library and file formats (LP, GNU MathProg, AMPL).

dropped.name: Full Adder
dropped.description: Three inputs, two outputs, five gates once the half-adder sum is shared: 10 literals against 18 for the unshared two-level pair.

dropped.name: Equality Comparator
dropped.description: A=B as an XOR tree feeding a NOR: 1+ceil(log2 n) depth, n XOR2s, and no carry chain — the only comparison that is not a prefix problem.

dropped.name: Shannon Expansion
dropped.description: f = x'·f|0 + x·f|1 read as hardware is a 2:1 mux; recurse to the leaves and you have literally built a ROM, a LUT, and the argument for functional decomposition.
source_headings: ## Shannon expansion: every function is a mux tree

dropped.name: Shannon Expansion
dropped.description: The cofactor identity f = !d.f_!d OR d.f_d that makes a LUT-alpha two LUT-(alpha-1) plus a MUX — and yields the cost bound L(n) ~ (4/3)2^(n-6) LUT6, doubling per input past the sixth.
dropped.spade_note: An algebraic identity plus a cost bound; the hardware it implies is the Fracturable LUT note.

dropped.description: Two adders plus shift multiplexers that fit inside the same basic logic element as the carry chain, yielding 15 selectable coefficients for the price of two bare adders — chosen so their distribution matches the network's actual weight histogram.
